prompts.title: Conversation and canvas
prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a high-fidelity, carefully composed desktop application UI design concept for Wright integrated inside the OpenAI desktop harness (called Codex here). This is a CONCEPT, not an actual screenshot. Landscape 16:9, target 1920x1080 or higher. Crisp readable typography, precise aligned controls, ample useful canvas space, convincingly restrained native desktop design. Fill almost the entire image with a straight-on app window; no laptop, desk, perspective, decorative gradients, glow, sci-fi, huge marketing headlines, glassmorphism or browser address bar. A narrow editorial footer OUTSIDE the app must say "WRIGHT × CODEX  ·  UI CONCEPT  ·  NOT IMPLEMENTED". Use friendly sans-serif like Inter/Segoe UI, charcoal-neutral surfaces (#181818, #212121, #282828), warm white text, quiet gray dividers, subtle rounded corners. Small teal only for Wright selection and graph ports; muted amber for needs-attention. Avoid current Wright's saturated navy panels and bright cyan buttons.
Host shell: two existing left areas, a slim 54px vertical icon rail for the desktop harness with restrained icons for chat, work, code, plugins and bottom settings; beside it a 188px Codex navigation list with "New chat", "Search", "Projects", and one fictional demo project "Engineering lab", plus just three short fictional chat titles. Preserve these TWO host navigation areas. No third persistent left navigation bar and no Wright activity rail. Clearly show host tab styling: simple rectangular document tabs across the right work area with close icons and a subtle selected state. ONE host-owned tab strip, never nested Wright document tabs. Do not imply changing the global host shell beyond layout selection.
Every view uses a compact Wright breadcrumb/workspace switcher with a small W mark and "Engineering lab", not a large second application banner. Never add a Wright chat composer, model picker, agent sidebar or memory controls. Use only fictional demo content. Avoid secrets, real conversations, technical hashes, runtime names, protocol labels and fake real-world success claims. Preserve workflow semantics: typed input/output sockets and clear connecting arrows, selection distinct from execution status, accepted source vs pending draft clearly distinguished. Button labels remain legible.

CONCEPT A — Conversation and canvas. Show a complete app at realistic desktop scale.
To the right of the TWO host navigation areas, a 330px native Codex conversation occupies the middle-left. Title "Prepare a replacement wheel". A short user bubble: "Create a preparation workflow for a 38 mm focus wheel." Assistant message: "The workflow is ready to inspect. Select a step to adjust its inputs and checks." Small compact workflow attachment card "Focus wheel · Draft". Only ONE native chat composer at the bottom, "Ask Codex…".
The remaining generous right 60% is the Wright work panel. Its HOST tab strip has "Workflows" inactive, "Focus wheel.wflow" active, and "requirements.md" inactive. Immediately below, a very compact toolbar: breadcrumb "W  Engineering lab / Focus wheel", muted "Saved", a discreet overflow menu. Second compact control row uses view selector "Diagram ▾", "+ Add step", "Inputs 3", "Results", Undo/Redo icons, "Check", and a restrained light "Run…" button. Avoid many header rows.
Main canvas is subtle dot-grid dark charcoal. Five elegant rectangular engineering nodes in two spacious rows connected in coherent order: "Requirements" (small subtext "38 mm · PETG") → "Create geometry" (subtext "CAD tool") → "Validate mesh"; then flow gently down to "Prepare print package" → "Review package". Typed colored sockets on left/right edges, thin graceful non-neon connectors. No fabricated active progress or completion ticks. One node "Create geometry" selected with thin teal border. All other nodes neutral. Keep node size readable, avoid tiny sprawling graph.
A contextual BOTTOM inspector drawer inside Wright's work area is OPEN, about 190px high and full canvas width. Header "Create geometry" with close icon; horizontal form sections "Purpose", "Inputs", and "Tool binding" rather than a right permanent column. Visible concise fields: "Diameter 38 mm", "Material PETG", "CAD provider: Choose…". Discreet "Apply changes" button. Demonstrate how selection details fit BELOW the canvas without stealing another vertical strip.
At the very bottom of Wright a thin collapsed row "Run details · Not started". Bottom-left zoom/fit icons remain inside canvas above drawer. In the editorial footer add the title "01  Conversation + canvas" and short subtitle "Two host rails · one chat · tools on demand". No extra annotation arrows.

CONCEPT B — Focused authoring. Same app aesthetic and same two host navigation areas, but native Codex chat is hidden using the host's full work view so the workflow fills the remaining width. A small native "Show chat" control sits in the app header; NO replacement chat pane or floating AI prompt field.
One HOST document tab strip has "Workflows", selected "Focus wheel.wflow", "requirements.md", and "mesh-report.html". Beneath it a single tight Wright toolbar: "W Engineering lab / Focus wheel", "Saved", view selector "Diagram ▾", "+ Add step", "Inputs", "Results", Undo, Redo, "Check", "Run…", overflow menu. "Source" and "Side by side" are options in the view selector, not another document tab strip.
The primary area is a large open workflow canvas taking about 80% of the work area with 5 readable nodes and flowing typed connections: "Requirements" (38 mm · PETG) → "Create geometry" → "Validate mesh" → "Prepare print package" → "Review package". Arrange spacious but efficient, connected across two rows, no giant empty dead areas. Subdued engineering line illustration of a small ridged focus wheel can appear as a thumbnail inside "Create geometry", not as dominant decoration. The "Validate mesh" node is selected, teal border. Node statuses are not run outcomes.
On the RIGHT ONLY, within the Wright panel, a 280px contextual inspector OPEN for "Validate mesh", with close and pin icons. Vertical sections: "Purpose", "Checks", "Inputs", "Advanced". Under Checks, simple configuration controls for "Diameter tolerance", "Manifold mesh", "Connected components". Clearly configuration, not completed validation evidence. Bottom buttons "Cancel" and "Apply". It is a temporary inspector, not a permanent tool rail.
Below the "+ Add step" toolbar control show a small elegant anchored POPOVER, approximately 215px wide and 270px tall, with search field "Find a step…" and only five clear rows: "Input", "AI task", "Tool action", "Validation", "Human review". It overlays the top-left corner of the canvas instead of forming a persistent left sidebar. Keep it from covering the main graph.
Bottom of canvas shows slim zoom controls, a collapsed minimap control and collapsed "Run details · Not started". In the editorial footer label "02  Focused authoring" and subtitle "Expand the work · reveal tools only when needed". Quiet, purposeful professional UI, no marketing widgets.

CONCEPT C — Run and review. Restore a 325px native Codex chat column between the two left host navigation areas and the right Wright panel. Use the same dark Codex visual system. This view shows a DIFFERENT engineering workflow, "Robot tracking diagnosis", not manufacturing. It illustrates a reusable working interface.
Host chat title "Investigate tracking drift". Fictional user bubble "Show the diagnostic evidence before I continue." Assistant text "The run is waiting at its declared review step. Compare the traces and record your decision in Wright." A small link-style card "Open tracking evidence". The ONE host composer remains at bottom "Ask Codex…". No agent permission prompts, terminal, or second chat.
ONE host tab strip on the right: "Workflows", "Tracking diagnosis.wflow", selected "Run 014", "tracking-report.html". Under it compact breadcrumb "W Engineering lab / Robot tracking diagnosis". Main header "Tracking diagnosis" with small "Run 014 · Revision 3" and amber pill "Waiting for review". Small action "Open workflow" near upper right. This state is explicitly fictional mock data, not a real run.
No node creation tools, no graph inspector, no new left sidebar. The working interface gives prime space to useful engineering evidence. Top half: wide clean chart card "Tracking error" with legible horizontal Time (s), vertical Error (mm), two plausible smooth traces labelled "Reference" and "Observed", a subtle anomaly region. Top right of chart card a small "Evidence" link. A quiet caption "Illustrative data" under the chart. Beneath: two compact evidence rows with file icons "tracking-report.html" and "sample-traces.csv", each with "View", subtle provenance "Analysis step · Revision 3". No claim real measurement thresholds passed.
Bottom half: spacious but compact declared review card with amber small heading "Review checkpoint", title "Review the diagnostic report", one sentence "Record a decision on this report revision." Fields "Decision" dropdown showing "Choose a decision…" and "Review notes". Main button "Record review"; small secondary link "View evidence". A fine muted note "Continuing is checked separately." No enormous approve-all or start-physical-operation button.
A thin progress strip near bottom "Inputs → Analysis → Review → Summary" with Review highlighted in amber and Summary visibly waiting. A collapsed bottom disclosure "Run details & history". Prefer the chart and review card to dominate over chrome. Footer title "03  Run + review" and subtitle "Same chat · task-specific view · durable Wright state".
